answer: An agent economy can limit Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it can earn reputation or vote. When a vertex submits a claim, independent agents can challenge it; if an audit proves coordinated identities fabricated evidence, the protocol forfeits their bonds and removes their accumulated standing. A cipher can bind each action to its bonded key, making evasion costly rather than merely changing names. Even across a tundra of cheap compute, the attacker must immobilize real capital per identity and risk losing it.
